parts.title: Rising Water
parts.text: For three days, rain hammered the valley, and Marisol watched the river creep up her street. Officials called the storm **unprecedented**, since no flood in a century had come close. Her neighbor Grant joined volunteers who stayed **vigilant** along the **levee**, a long earthen wall built to hold the river back, scanning for leaks. By the third evening, everyone's sense of safety felt **tenuous**, like a thread stretched too far.

parts.title: The Breach
parts.text: At midnight, a **surge** of brown water pushed over a weak section and began to **inundate** the lower streets. Families hurried to the high school gym with bags and pets, and the room soon filled with damp coats and anxious whispers. Inside, a nurse used **triage**, treating the most urgent injuries before the minor ones, while Marisol handed out dry socks and warm tea.

parts.title: Neighbors
parts.text: By morning the water had stopped rising, and Marisol, Grant and their classmate Tamika decided to **mobilize** their school. Tamika built a volunteer schedule, and within a day two hundred students were sorting supplies. A **charitable** foundation sent trucks of food, and local stores chose to **donate** blankets and bottled water. In the **aftermath**, the work shifted toward repairs, because it would take months to **reconstruct** the homes and the ruined bridge.

parts.title: Higher Ground
parts.text: Weeks later, the river was calm again, and the levee had been rebuilt higher. Grant joked that the new wall looked like a small mountain. Marisol thought about how fear had turned into action. The flood had exposed the town's weak points, but it had also revealed its strength: people who barely knew each other had shared food, tools and time. She kept her volunteer badge on her backpack as a reminder.
